explanation.text: The Logic: A call option is "in-the-money" (ITM) when the spot price of the underlying is above the strike price, giving the call positive intrinsic value (spot − strike). Strike > spot is out-of-the-money (OTM); strike = spot is at-the-money (ATM). Note: Option moneyness (ITM/ATM/OTM) is not defined in the PMS Distributors (XXI-A) derivatives chapter, which covers definitions of forwards/futures/options/swaps and PMS-derivative permissions only. Treat this as general option theory; in-depth options content is in NISM Series VIII.
